lane-runtime.d: Which vLLM code actually runs in the container. In the DeepSeek recipe there are three: A · Anemll (prebuilt image, default), B · Stage-C overlay (whole files copied over another base) and C · official-main (experiment). The same knob can exist in one lane and be a no-op in another.

headless-rank.d: A rank of a multi-node vLLM server that only executes the model (GPU + NCCL), with no HTTP API or scheduler of its own; it receives its work from rank 0. Enabled with --headless.

exit-code-3.d: Contract of the DeepSeek launcher: exiting with 3 means the ranks are already up (for example, restored by restart: unless-stopped after a reboot). Supervisors treat it as success (SuccessExitStatus=3) instead of retrying.

preflight-check.d: Running a patcher in check-only mode, in a throwaway container (docker compose run --rm --no-deps), before bringing up any rank. If the source doesn't match, the boot stops without leaving the pair half-patched.

block-k.d: Opt-in hotfix of the DeepSeek recipe (DSPARK_ENABLE_DSPARK_BLOCK_K=1) that exempts the dspark method from the k % n_predict divisibility rule, allowing k=5 (the trained block) instead of k=6. Measured +2–10% in single-stream.

kill-switch.d: An environment variable that turns a code path on or off at runtime. In the DeepSeek recipe, the VLLM_DSPARK_* variables are real kill-switches only in the Stage-C lane; in the Anemll image they are not registered and only produce a warning.

atencao-dp.d: Running the attention layers in data parallel: each GPU serves its own requests and keeps only their KV, instead of splitting heads with TP. With MLA, whose single latent is replicated on every TP rank, it avoids storing the same KV N times. It is usually paired with expert parallelism for the MoE layers (DeepInfer: EP64·DP64).

eplb.d: Places extra copies of the busiest experts on the GPUs of an EP group so that no GPU becomes the straggler of the all-to-all. DeepInfer runs the 384 routed experts of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash plus 32 redundant ones on 4 GPUs, and plus 64 on 64 GPUs.

anel-sem-switch.d: Four or more nodes cabled in a loop, each node's two ports going to its two neighbors, with no switch. A node across the ring is reached through a relayed hop, so rank placement and the collective algorithm must follow the cabling (TensorFold's 0-1-3-2 order; SGLang's patched sparkring NCCL).

desagregacao-prefill-decode.d: Serving prefill and decode on separate GPU pools, sized independently, with the KV handed from one to the other. Prefill is compute-bound and decode is bound by bandwidth and latency, so each pool gets its own parallelism and batch size (DeepInfer benchmarks 4 GPUs for prefill and 64 for decode).

dominio-scale-up.d: The set of GPUs joined by the fast GPU-to-GPU fabric (NVLink/NVSwitch), as opposed to the scale-out network (InfiniBand or RoCE) between domains. An 8-GPU HGX node is one; rack-scale systems extend it to dozens of GPUs. Collectives inside it are much cheaper than across it.
